lockState.searchScope: the full recursive git tree at the pinned revision (175 blobs)
lockState.declaredRangeStyle: caret ranges for the Angular packages and most runtime dependencies, tilde ranges for the test toolchain, and one exact pin (typescript 2.4)
lockState.packageManagerMismatch: The repository ships a yarn lockfile while its README offers `npm install` as an equally valid path. npm would ignore yarn.lock entirely and resolve the ranges fresh. This unit installed with yarn precisely so that the committed pin was honoured.
lockState.consequence: The closure IS pinned by the repository. Installing with yarn and --frozen-lockfile reproduces the 2017 resolution rather than resolving ranges against today's registry.

integrityAlgorithms: sha1 (as a URL fragment on the resolved field)
committedLockAnalysis.integrityNote: yarn lockfile v1 as written in 2017 carries no separate `integrity` field; the sha1 fragment appended to the resolved URL is the whole of its content addressing. Every one of the 963 entries carries one. sha512 subresource integrity postdates this lockfile and is absent by construction, not by omission.

observedInstall.what: The dependency tree yarn 1.3.2 materialised from the committed lockfile in the declared cell on 2026-08-11.
observedInstall.frozenLockfileNote: `--frozen-lockfile` makes yarn fail rather than update the lockfile if the manifest and the lock disagree. It exited 0, so the committed lock satisfies the committed manifest exactly, and no lockfile write occurred.
observedInstall.directoryCountNote: 1149 counts every package directory including nested node_modules; 828 is the top level of a flattened yarn install. Neither number is the lockfile entry count (963), because yarn hoists and because some lock entries share a single installed directory.

resolutionNote: These are the versions the committed lockfile pins, confirmed by reading package.json out of each installed package after the frozen install. They are not a fresh range resolution.

warningsObserved.unmetPeerDependencies: 2 — @angular/flex-layout@2.0.0-beta.10-4905443 declares peer dependencies on @angular/core ~4.4.4 and @angular/common ~4.4.4, while the application runs 5.0.3.

lifecycleScripts.why: node-sass 4.5.3 is a required build input — .angular-cli.json declares styles.scss as the global stylesheet and three components use .scss — so its install lifecycle must run for the production build to be attemptable at all. Disabling scripts would have guaranteed a failure that says nothing about the fixture.
lifecycleScripts.outcome: node-sass resolved a prebuilt darwin-x64-57 binding (the Node 8 ABI) rather than compiling from source; node_modules/node-sass/vendor/darwin-x64-57 exists.
lifecycleScripts.consequence: The install contacted GitHub release assets in addition to the yarn registry. That host is on the baseline allowlist in attempt.json.

supplyChainReachability.basisOfClaim: the frozen install completed with exit status 0, which requires every one of the 963 locked tarballs to have been fetched and its sha1 to have matched
supplyChainReachability.note: A 2017 yarn lockfile resolving completely in 2026 is a finding worth stating plainly: nothing in this closure has been unpublished or had its sha1 drift.

closureShaNote: The closure digest is the sha256 of the committed yarn.lock itself, because the pin lives upstream. No generated lockfile was produced by this unit.
nonclaims: Per-artifact byte digests were not independently mirrored; the recorded content addresses are the sha1 fragments the committed lockfile declares.
A resolvable closure establishes no browser behavior, no licence compatibility of transitive dependencies, no migration feasibility, and no production readiness.
Nothing here claims the sha1 content addressing in a 2017 yarn lockfile is cryptographically adequate by present-day standards. It is recorded as what the era pinned with.
